source_refs.note: Topic 2.7.5, printed pages 36-38: box diagrams (Figures 2.13 and 2.14) and Table 2.7, given in two tables with the argon core abbreviated.

blocks.text: A useful way of representing electronic configurations is a diagram that places electrons in boxes. Each box represents an atomic orbital; the boxes are arranged in order of increasing energy from bottom to top; an electron is an arrow whose direction shows its spin; and when two electrons occupy an orbital their spins are opposite, so the two arrows in a box point in opposite directions. Electrons in the same region of space repel each other because they have the same charge, so wherever possible electrons occupy separate orbitals of the same subshell to minimise the repulsion, with the same spins in different orbitals; they pair only when no empty orbital is left within the subshell. The electronic structures of carbon, nitrogen and oxygen illustrate this: carbon's two 2p electrons and nitrogen's three each occupy separate orbitals, and only in oxygen is a fourth electron forced to pair.

blocks.title: Reading the table
blocks.text: [Ar] stands for the argon core 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6, which the printed table writes out in full for each element from potassium to krypton. Chromium (3d5 4s1) and copper (3d10 4s1) are printed as shown: a half-filled or fully filled d subshell is preferred.

blocks.prompt: Write the box diagram, in words, for the valence electrons of phosphorus (Z = 15), obeying Hund's rule and the Pauli principle.
blocks.explanation: Phosphorus is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3. Its valence electrons are the 3s pair, one box with an up and a down arrow, and the three 3p electrons, one up arrow in each of the three boxes px, py and pz, unpaired with parallel spins.

items: Box diagrams: one box per orbital, ordered by energy upward, arrows for spins, opposite arrows when paired; electrons spread over a subshell's orbitals before pairing (C two singly, N three singly, O one pair).
Table 2.7 lists the ground-state configurations of Z = 1 to 36; 4s fills before 3d, and Cr and Cu take 3d5 4s1 and 3d10 4s1.
